stemMd: A music venue will sell more tickets by adding a second performance of a sold-out show. It predicts that total attendance across both performances will double. Which assumption is required?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Every attendee will attend both performances.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Demand at the offered times and prices is sufficient to fill both performances.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The venue will spend nothing on advertising.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The first performance sold out quickly.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Both performances will last the same length.

explanationMd: One sellout establishes demand for at least one full house, not two. Doubling total attendance requires enough demand to fill the added capacity without leaving seats empty in either performance.

distractorRationale.d: Speed of the first sellout does not quantify unmet demand.
distractorRationale.e: Duration does not establish that both sell out.
distractorRationale.a: Two full audiences need not consist of the same people.
distractorRationale.c: Advertising cost is irrelevant to the attendance prediction.
